newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money steady on Central Bank cue.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money steady on Central Bank cue.

text.p: Manila overnight money was unchanged at an average rate of 10.03125 percent on Tuesday after the Central Bank kept its overnight borrowing rate at 10 percent, dealers said.
"People were expecting the Central Bank to change its rates," a foreign bank dealer said. The expectations were triggered by a rise in T-bill rates at the regular weekly auction on Monday.
Rates were wedged from 10.25 to 10.03125 percent, with 25 lenders and 18 borrowers.
The secondary market continued to see tepid trading as banks decided to hold back to see if domestic interest rates would rise.
"There was some activity but not in big volumes. People are just buying to meet clients' requirements," a dealer said.
Interest rates are expected to correct upward after reaching very low levels, he said.
Another dealer said banks were also apprehensive in buying T-bills in big volumes because of the scheduled remittance of billion of pesos in tax payments early next week.
A Reuters poll of eight financial institutions gave bid rates of 10.20 to 10.40 percent for the three-month bills.
